messages.subject: yearlySiteCovs in gdistsamp(lambdaformula=)
parts:
I'm pretty sure I've already got the answer to this reading between the lines of the other gdistsamp questions asked here. But just to be clear and to possibly help others in the future. 

Can you use yearlySiteCovs in the lambda argument of gdistsamp?

When I plug in the yearlySiteCovs into phi or p it works, but it doesn't for lambda. So I'm guessing it just isn't allowed. 

What I'm trying to do is use changing water levels in wetlands over time to explain abundance, and the water levels change with each survey. But maybe gdistsamp isn't the right framework in that case. 

I welcome any comments. 

Auriel

messages.subject: Re: yearlySiteCovs in gdistsamp(lambdaformula=)
parts:
Ariel,

My vague understanding of gdistsamp is that yearly site covariates within the function are equivalent to visit covariates as traditionally considered.  Consequently (because super-abundance is considered closed), lambda cannot vary as function of yearly site covs (although availability and detection can).  In other words, the population is considered 'open' with regards to movement and temporary immigration that makes certain individuals unavailable for detection, but closed with regards to the super-population of individuals that might possibly use a site during a series of surveys.  I guess 'true' robust-design distance sampling has now been formally described (Sollman et al. 2015), but do not know if (do not believe that) this is yet supported in unmarked.   If population growth/decline/size across years is of interest, perhaps you might stack the yearly data and include a factorial covariate for year?

John
